title: Best Running Shoes for Beginners in India (2026)
summary: Three first running shoes for India: Kalenji Run Active, Puma Electrify NITRO 4 and Velocity NITRO 5, based on shop pages and maker guides.
description: Helps new runners in India pick a first pair: Kalenji Run Active, Puma Electrify NITRO 4 and Velocity NITRO 5, compared from shop pages and guides.
lead: Compare three road-running options: a shoe listed for occasional jogging, a neutral daily road shoe and a model positioned for frequent runners. Choose by fit and intended use. We checked manufacturer specifications and have not run in these shoes.

picks.name: Kalenji Run Active (men's, Comfort Fit)
picks.label: For first-timers
picks.verdict: An option for light, occasional jogging within the maker’s stated workload.
paragraphs: Decathlon India lists the men's Run Active for occasional road or path running up to 10 km a week. Its published technical details give a 10 mm drop and 245 g in size 8.5. Those figures describe this version and size; they are not a fit guarantee.

The listing describes heel cushioning and a flexible sole. We see it as an option to compare for light jogging rather than a shoe chosen for high weekly mileage. Try your normal running socks and check the current size chart. We have not run in this shoe.
good: Published use limit makes its intended workload clear.
The listing provides both a drop and a size-specific weight.
not_good: The stated use is occasional running, not high-mileage training.
Fit and comfort need a try-on; specifications cannot settle them.
picks.search_query: Kalenji Run Active men running shoes

picks.name: Puma Electrify NITRO 4 (men's, road)
picks.label: For everyday road runs
picks.verdict: A neutral everyday road shoe that Puma's own beginner guide lists for new runners. Its page gives the drop and stack height.
paragraphs: Puma describes the fourth Electrify as a daily shoe for road runners. The Puma India page lists a regular fit, neutral support and an engineered mesh upper with breathable and stretch zones. The midsole mixes NITROFOAM, a lightweight foam, with PROFOAMLITE, an EVA foam. The outsole is PUMAGRIP rubber.

The page lists a 10 mm heel-to-toe drop and a stack height of 35 mm at the heel and 25 mm at the front. Puma's beginner guide lists this shoe for new runners and for short to medium-distance training. That is the maker's own view, not an independent one. This is the men's road version.
good: Puma India lists neutral support, a 10 mm drop and a 35 mm / 25 mm stack height, so the key specs are on the page.
Puma's beginner guide lists it for new runners and for short to medium-distance training.
The Puma page lists an engineered mesh upper and a PUMAGRIP rubber outsole.
not_good: The page does not give the weight or say how soft the cushioning is.
Stock can depend on the colour and size you want.
picks.search_query: Puma Electrify NITRO 4 men running shoes

picks.name: Puma Velocity NITRO 5 (men's, road)
picks.label: For regular runners
picks.verdict: A neutral daily trainer with medium cushioning and an 8 mm drop on its page. It may be more shoe than you need if you are not sure you will keep running.
paragraphs: The Puma India page lists NITROFOAM cushioning, an engineered mesh upper and a PUMAGRIP outsole. The details list shows road running, neutral pronation (no extra support built in for feet that roll inward), medium cushioning and an 8 mm heel-to-toe drop.  Puma also sells a Wide version.

Puma's beginner guide says the Velocity NITRO suits 5K and 10K training and first-race preparation. The details list marks the runner type as Frequent, so a person who runs only now and then may prefer a simpler shoe.
good: Puma's beginner guide says it suits 5K and 10K training and first-race preparation.
Puma sells a Wide version of the same shoe, which may help if regular shoes feel tight across the front of the foot.
not_good: The details list the runner type as Frequent, so it may suit regular runners better than very occasional ones.
picks.search_query: Puma Velocity NITRO 5 men running shoes

choose.heading: Fit comes first
choose.text: Nike's running guide says to leave about a thumb's width between your big toe and the end of the shoe. Puma's guide says about the same and adds that you should try shoes with the socks you will run in. Puma says a slightly bigger shoe is better than a tight one.

choose.heading: Try shoes on later in the day
choose.text: Nike's guide says feet tend to widen through the day. So a shoe that fits in the morning may feel tight in the evening. If you can, try shoes on in the afternoon or evening.

choose.heading: Pick a road shoe for road running
choose.text: Nike's guide says road shoes suit pavement, and trail shoes give extra grip on uneven ground. Puma's guide says a normal road shoe is usually enough for flat, dry paths. Check that the page says road running.

choose.heading: Neutral or stability
choose.text: A neutral shoe has no extra support built in. A stability shoe adds support. Puma's guide says comfort matters more than technical terms for first-time runners. It describes ForeverRun NITRO as its stability shoe. If you are unsure which type you need, a shoe shop can help you decide.

choose.heading: Read the maker's stated use
choose.text: Decathlon says the Run Active is for up to 10 km a week. Puma's Velocity NITRO 5 page marks the runner type as Frequent. These notes tell you when a shoe may be too simple, or more than you need.

choose.heading: Check the exact listing before paying
choose.text: Check the current seller listing for availability, delivery to your pincode, returns and warranty coverage before ordering.

faq.q: Which of these is the easiest first pair?
faq.a: The Run Active is listed for occasional running up to 10 km a week. The Electrify NITRO 4 is another road-running option to try. Choose by comfort, fit and expected use, rather than by the most technical specification.

faq.q: Do I need a stability shoe as a beginner?
faq.a: Puma's guide says comfort matters more than technical terms for first-time runners. This is general advice and not a fitting. A shoe shop can help you decide.

It is how much higher the heel sits than the front of the shoe. Puma's guide says beginners need not think about it much. The Puma pages list 10 mm for the Electrify NITRO 4 and 8 mm for the Velocity NITRO 5.

faq.q: How do I know when to replace my shoes?
faq.a: Inspect wear, grip and changes in comfort. A maker’s mileage estimate is not a guaranteed lifespan or a replacement schedule for every runner. Ask a running shop for help assessing a worn pair.

faq.q: Should I buy online or in a store?
faq.a: A store is better for fit, because you can try the shoe on.
